mutations.defect: closing </html> tag removed
a <script> tag, so the page no longer ships zero JS
a CTA pointing at a host that cannot resolve
a 2000px fixed-width element, far wider than the 375px viewport
body copy at #bbbbbb on white, under the AA contrast floor
an em dash in rendered copy
one digit removed from a tel: href while its label still reads correctly
a tel: href written with spaces, so the digits match but the URI is malformed
an embedded image large enough to push the page past its byte budget
a coloured stripe down one edge of a callout, the generated-UI callout tell
an image placeholder left in the src, so the page renders a broken image
the brief's accent hex replaced everywhere by a nearby darker tone
an entrance start state with no animation to bring it back, so the text never appears
content removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion instead of just its motion
a paragraph allowed to run the full viewport width, far past 80 characters a line
every element forced to one size, so the page has no scale
a small tracked-out all-caps label, the eyebrow kicker
a label set in small caps, the same kicker in a serif costume
a section heading prefixed with a number and a separator
every call to action pushed below the fold at both viewports, so the first screen sells nothing
a second call to action above the fold, the hedge the hero rule refuses
the direction on record says the opposite theme from the one the page renders

knownBlindSpots.defect: a claim in the copy that appears nowhere in the brief, such as the drafter's invented "the keys stay with you" and "no term, no penalty"
knownBlindSpots.whyMissed: checking a sentence against a brief is a judgement, not a comparison; nothing deterministic can decide it
knownBlindSpots.caughtBy: the advisory review pass, which is why that pass exists

knownBlindSpots.defect: a page that is stranded in one column, or repeats one formula down the page, or wears the stock skeleton in a new dress, while clearing every measurable check
knownBlindSpots.whyMissed: the ink-based metrics catch what they name (a stranded section, a flat scale, a long measure, a missing call to action) and nothing else; whether a page is well composed is still a judgement
knownBlindSpots.caughtBy: the composition judge, which looks at the rendered tiles and can buy two layout repairs, and never decides the verdict
